title: NodeBits: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Accelerating Graph Inference by Post-Hoc Binary Quantization

problem.claim: GNN inference is expensive because node-feature propagation and aggregation are repeated across layers, with cost increasing with graph size.

gap.claim: Existing GNN-to-MLP distillation methods require manually tuned vector-quantization parameters and an additional MLP training stage.

contributions.claim: NodeBits is a plug-and-play framework that accelerates graph inference through post-hoc binary quantization.
DaBQ is a data-aware binary quantizer that uses lightweight node-representation statistics to reduce information loss from binarization.
NodeBits* fine-tunes the readout layer to further offset binarization-related information loss.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the post-hoc binary quantization scheme as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across 20 benchmark datasets, NodeBits reportedly achieves accuracy comparable to full-precision GNN inference while being orders of magnitude faster.
The authors report that NodeBits surpasses existing GNN-to-MLP methods in accuracy and inference speed.
NodeBits is reported to maintain competitive predictive performance with negligible accuracy drop and to apply directly to trained GNN models.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs are widely used for graph learning, but their inference cost grows with graph size.
Existing GNN-to-MLP approaches reduce inference cost with vector quantization but add tuning requirements and an extra training stage.
NodeBits introduces post-hoc binary quantization, with DaBQ discretizing node representations into compact bit strings using data-aware statistics.
The framework reconstructs embeddings from bit strings and sends them to the pretrained readout layer without training an additional MLP; NodeBits* optionally fine-tunes that layer.
Experiments on 20 benchmark datasets report accuracy comparable to full-precision inference, substantially higher speed, and improvements over existing GNN-to-MLP methods.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the detailed quantization algorithm or reconstruction procedure.
The abstract does not provide per-dataset results, baselines, hardware settings, or reproducibility details.
